raw_text:
Here is a concise, fully integrated 12-week muscle-gain plan for your vegan client, incorporating: 4-day resistance split (Push, Pull, Legs, Upper/Lower), Phase structure with progression, cardio, nutrition targets (120–150 g protein emphasis, 150 g target), a weekly cheat meal day, post-workout meals, protein powder guidance, and Phase 3 push-intensity specifics. It’s written to be handed to a client or used as a trainer-facing summary.

Client profile recap
- Age: 26
- Sex: presumably female
- Goals: muscle gain
- Diet: strict vegan (no animals, fish, eggs, dairy)
- Training history: recreational lifter with full gym access
- Protein target: ~150 g/day from plant sources
- Additional notes: 4-day resistance split, cardio integrated, one weekly vegan cheat meal day

Overall plan at a glance
- Duration: 12 weeks
- Training split: 4 days per week
  - Day A: Push
  - Day B: Pull
  - Day C: Legs
  - Day D: Upper/Lower accessory or full-body
- Phases:
  - Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Foundation and technique, moderate volume, hypertrophy base
  - Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 — Hypertrophy intensification, higher volume and progression
  - Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 — Peak hypertrophy with elevated push intensity, density work, and advanced techniques
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions/week, 20–30 minutes, mostly Zone 2 easy to moderate; optional higher-intensity session every 1–2 weeks depending on recovery
- Cheat meal day: once per week, vegan-compliant, structured to sustain adherence and recovery
- Nutrition: ~150 g protein/day; slight caloric surplus +250–500 kcal/day; focus on leucine-rich plant proteins; protein timing around workouts
- Supplements: vegan protein powder, creatine monohydrate (5 g/day), B12, D3 (vegan), omega-3 (algal oil), vitamin D as needed

Weekly training structure (typical template)
- Monday: Push
- Tuesday: Pull
- Wednesday: Cardio (optional mobility)
- Thursday: Legs
- Friday: Upper/Lower accessory
- Saturday: Cardio or rest (depending on fatigue)
- Sunday: Rest or light mobility

Phase 1: Foundation and technique (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: establish technique, build work capacity, and set up for progressive overload.

Weeks 1–2
- Day A – Push
  - Barbell bench press: 3 x 8–10
  - Overhead press (standing): 3 x 8–10
  - Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 10–12
  - Dumbbell lateral raises: 3 x 12–15
  - Triceps: skull crushers or pushdowns: 3 x 12–15
  - Push-ups or incline push-ups: 2 x 12–15
- Day B – Pull
  - Bent-over barbell row: 3 x 8–10
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
  - Seated cable row: 3 x 10–12
  - Dumbbell bicep curls: 3 x 12–15
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Day C – Legs
  - Back squat or goblet squat: 3 x 8–10
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8–10
  - Leg press: 3 x 10–12
  - Leg extension: 3 x 12–15
  - Hamstring curl: 3 x 12–15
  - Calf raises: 3 x 15–20
- Day D – Upper/Full body accessory
  - Romanian deadlift or rack pulls: 3 x 6–8
  - Dumbbell rows: 3 x 8–10
  - Dumbbell chest fly: 3 x 10–12
  - Core circuit: planks 3 x 30–45s, side planks 2 x 30s
  - Optional conditioning: 15–20 min low-intensity cardio
- Cardio: 2 sessions, 20–25 min Zone 2
- Cheat meal day: not yet emphasized; keep regular structure overall

Weeks 3–4
- Increase load subtly (~2.5–5% if technique solid)
- Push: add 1 more set to main lifts if form remains strong
- Pull: add 1 set or an extra exercise
- Legs: progress squat load with tempo emphasis (eccentric 3 seconds)
- Day D: maintain structure; add one core exercise
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions; one tempo interval optional
- Nutrition: continue protein target; maintain slight surplus

Phase 2: Hypertrophy intensification (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: higher volume, progressive overload, refine symmetry.

Weeks 5–6
- Day A – Push
  - Barbell bench press: 4 x 6–8
  - Overhead press: 4 x 6–8
  - Dumbbell incline press: 3 x 8–10
  - Dips (assisted if needed): 3 x 8–10
  - Cable lateral raises: 3 x 12–15
  - Tricep pushdowns: 3 x 12–15
- Day B – Pull
  - Barbell row: 4 x 6–8
  - Pull-ups/assisted: 4 x 6–8
  - Seated cable row: 3 x 8–10
  - Dumbbell hammer curls: 3 x 10–12
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Day C – Legs
  - Back squat: 4 x 6–8
  - Romanian deadlift: 4 x 8–10
  - Leg press: 3 x 10–12
  - Leg extensions: 3 x 12–15
  - Hamstring curls: 3 x 12–15
  - Calf raises: 4 x 15–20
- Day D – Upper/Full body accessory
  - Hip thrusts/glute bridge: 3 x 8–10
  - Lat pulldown variants: 3 x 8–10
  - Chest-supported row: 3 x 10–12
  - Core circuit: 3 rounds

Weeks 7–8
- Push: maintain 4 x 5–7 on main presses; keep accessory volume
- Pull: 4 x 5–7 on rows/chins; add heavier pull movement
- Legs: 4 x 5–7 squats; maintain posterior chain volume
- Day D: 3–4 sets of accessories
- Cardio: 2 sessions of 25–30 min; one higher effort if appetite permits
- Recovery: mobility and soft-tissue work continued

Phase 3: Peak hypertrophy and overload (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: maximize muscle gain via elevated push intensity, density, and occasional advanced techniques.

Weeks 9–10
- Push
  - Barbell bench press: 5 x 5–6 at 85–90% 1RM
  - Overhead press: 4 x 6–8 at 75–85% 1RM
  - Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 8–10
  - Dips (weighted if capable): 3 x 6–8
  - Lateral raises: 3 x 12–15
  - Tricep pushdowns/skull crushers: 3 x 12–15
  - Optional push finisher: push-ups or incline push-ups 1–2 sets; cable face pulls 2 x 15–20
  - Tempo: 2–0–1–1 on main lifts; occasional slower eccentric (3–4s) on one set weekly
- Pull
  - Not modified here; see standard Phase 3 pull template
- Legs
  - Maintain or a lighter day; focus remains on push intensity
- Upper/Lower or accessory day: maintain balanced volume
- Cardio: minimal to moderate; 1–2 sessions easy
- Nutrition: protein ~150 g; calories +250–500 as needed; carbs around push day optimized

Weeks 11–12
- Push
  - Bench: 4–5 x 4–6 at 85–90% 1RM
  - Overhead press: 4 x 5–7
  - Incline press: 3 x 6–8
  - Dips: 3 x 6–8
  - Lateral raises: 3 x 12–15
  - Tricep work: 3 x 10–12
  - Core: 3 rounds
  - Optional density set on bench (clusters)
- Pull
  - 4–5 x 4–6 rows; weighted chin-ups 4 x 6–8
  - Seated row: 3 x 8–10
  - Biceps: 3 x 10–12
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Legs
  - 4–5 x 5 on back squat; 4 x 6–8 RDL; 3 x 8–10 leg extension/hams
  - Calves: 4 x 15–20
- Cardio: optional, keep light to moderate if muscle gains are priority
- Deload option: if signs of fatigue appear, taper volume for Week 12

Phase 3 push intensity adjustments (summary)
- Main lifts moved to heavier sets with 85–90% 1RM range
- Tempo: consistent controlled tempo; occasional slower eccentrics and pauses
- Advanced techniques: tempo variations, drop sets, cluster sets, pre/post-exhaust methods
- Density and frequency: push work remains high intensity with slightly reduced accessory volume on peak weeks to preserve recovery
- Progression: weekly overload target on main push lifts; monitor RPE (7–9 range)

Cheat meal day integration (summary)
- Frequency: once per week on a consistent day (e.g., Saturday)
- Structure: high-protein breakfast and meals leading into a larger vegan indulgence meal
- Protein target: aim for 140–170 g total protein on cheat days if appetite allows
- Calories: add ~600–1,000 extra calories from carbs and fats, depending on goals
- Post-cheat: return to normal protein targets next day; light activity or mobility can aid recovery
- Plan ahead: have a few vegan cheat-day meals planned to maximize nutrition density

Post-workout meals (examples)
- 25–40 g protein post-workout: tofu scramble bowl, tempeh wrap, high-protein smoothie, chickpea-quinoa bowl, or tempeh stir-fry with noodles
- Carbs: 40–60 g carbs post-workout if energy demands were high
- Fats: 5–15 g in post-workout meals to support satiety and overall nutrition
- Timing: 1–2 hours after training; shakes can be used immediately if appetite is low

Protein powder recommendations (summary)
- Primary options: pea+rice blends or soy protein isolate for rapid amino delivery
- Soy-free options: pea+rice+hemp blends
- Considerations: taste, digestibility, added sugars, third-party testing
- Use: 1–2 scoops daily depending on protein target; post-workout and/or meals to hit daily protein

Cardio integration (summary)
- 2–3 sessions/week, 20–30 minutes
- Zone 2 for base sessions; occasional tempo or interval session every 1–2 weeks
- Optional longer easy cardio on off days
- Hydration and protein around cardio: ensure post-workout protein; adjust calories if needed

Measurement and progression tracking
- Track main lift weights, reps, and RPE weekly
- Take body measurements: chest, arms, waist, thighs every 4 weeks
- Photos every 4 weeks
- Adjust calories if weight gain exceeds 0.25–0.5 kg per week or if fat gain is a concern
- Recovery metrics: sleep 7–9 hours; monitor energy levels and soreness

What I can customize next
- Equipment-specific Phase 3 day-by-day templates (Push, Pull, Legs, Day D)
- A precise 12-week week-by-week, day-by-day plan with exact sets/reps, tempo, RPE targets
- A 7–14 day rotating vegan cheat-day menu with macro targets
- A printable one-page plan or spreadsheet for client handout
- A tailored post-workout meal plan with exact gram targets per meal based on her preferences

If you’d like, I can generate a fully detailed, day-by-day 12-week plan with exact exercise selections, sets/reps, tempo, rest periods, and integrated cardio, plus a high-level nutrition week-by-week guide aligned to her equipment and taste preferences. Share any constraints (equipment list, injuries, preferred exercises) and I’ll tailor and deliver.
